cohort: The study included 199 patients (156 staged, 43 simultaneous) who underwent bilateral total hip arthroplasty between 2017 and 2020.
finding: Simultaneous bilateral total hip arthroplasty was found to be non-inferior to staged implants in terms of safety (local/systemic complications, readmission rates) and patient satisfaction, although the incidence of postoperative anemia was significantly higher in the simultaneous group.
